title: Domestic Flights in Türkiye: Turkish Airlines, Pegasus & AJet Compared
seoTitle: Domestic Flights in Türkiye: THY, Pegasus & AJet (2026)
metaDescription: Compare Turkish Airlines, Pegasus, and AJet domestic baggage rules, IST vs SAW hubs, peak-season booking windows, and tight connection strategies.
quickAnswer: Turkish Airlines operates its domestic network from Istanbul Airport (IST) on the European side, while low-cost carriers Pegasus and AJet run their primary Istanbul hubs out of Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) on the Asian side. All three include 15 kg of checked baggage on standard domestic entry tiers, though cabin rules and fare flexibility differ sharply.
category: Practical Travel Logistics, Money, Visas & Transport

body.text: How do baggage allowances differ between Turkish Airlines, Pegasus and AJet?

All three carriers operate domestic routes on a weight concept, starting at 15 kg of checked luggage on standard domestic entry packages (EcoFly on Turkish Airlines, Saver on Pegasus, and Basic on AJet). Where travelers get caught out is cabin baggage, seat fees, and connecting from an international 23 kg allowance down to a domestic 15 kg limit.
Check each carrier's official 2026 rules before you book:

Watch out for excess weight and oversize charges at the counter. Turkish Airlines charges 1,000 TRY for domestic oversized pieces over 158 cm linear dimensions per its [checked baggage policy](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-tr/any-questions/checked-baggage/), while [AJet's excess baggage table](https://ajet.com/en/corporate/rules-and-conditions/excess-baggage) charges 750 TRY online versus 850 TRY at the airport per additional 5 kg. On international legs, both [Pegasus's Light Package](https://www.flypgs.com/en/pegasus-baggage-allowance) and [AJet's Basic Package](https://ajet.com/en/corporate/rules-and-conditions/baggage) strip away overhead cabin bags entirely, leaving only a 40×30×15 cm underseat bag—so never assume your international and domestic legs share the same cabin allowance.
Which airline uses IST vs SAW airport in Istanbul?

Turkish Airlines flies almost all its domestic routes from Istanbul Airport (IST) on the northern European side, whereas Pegasus Airlines and AJet (Turkish Airlines' low-cost subsidiary, formerly AnadoluJet) operate their main Istanbul hubs from Sabiha Gökçen International Airport (SAW) on the Asian side. The two airports sit roughly 76 km apart across the Bosphorus.

Choosing the wrong airport can wipe out a €25 ticket saving in transfer time and taxi fares, as outlined in [IST vs SAW transit comparisons](https://www.alwantr.com/en/blog/istanbul-airport-vs-sabiha-gokcen/). Match your airport to your stay:

items: Pick IST (Turkish Airlines) if you are connecting off a long-haul Star Alliance or full-service international flight, or staying in European-side hubs like Sultanahmet, Beyoğlu, Şişli, or Beşiktaş (linked by the M11 metro and Havaist shuttles).

Pick SAW (Pegasus or AJet) if you are staying in Kadıköy, Moda, or Üsküdar on the Asian side (linked directly by the M4 metro), or flying point-to-point to Kayseri (ASR), Nevşehir (NAV), İzmir (ADB), Antalya (AYT), Dalaman (DLM), or Bodrum (BJV).

Skip flying altogether for Istanbul–Ankara or Istanbul–Konya if your hotel is near Kadıköy—the [YHT high-speed train](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/trains-in-turkey-guide) is often faster door-to-door.

body.text: How early should you book domestic legs in peak season?

For peak travel months—May through June, September through October, and Turkish national holidays (Ramazan Bayramı and Kurban Bayramı)—book domestic flights 6 to 10 weeks ahead. On thin regional routes with limited daily frequencies, such as Istanbul to Nevşehir (NAV) for Cappadocia or Van (VAN), fares double and morning departures sell out a month before travel.

In July and August, coastal routes to Bodrum, Dalaman, and Antalya spike every Friday afternoon and Sunday evening as Istanbul residents head south for the weekend. If you are building a multi-stop route that mixes flights with [renting a car on the Aegean or Turquoise Coast](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/renting-a-car-in-turkey), lock in your domestic flight times first before committing to non-refundable hotel nights or car pickups.
How do you handle tight international-to-domestic connections?

Never book a self-transfer between IST and SAW with less than 6 hours between scheduled arrival and departure—Bosphorus traffic alone can eat two hours, and you must clear passport control, claim bags, and re-check in. Even within the same airport, self-transferring on separate tickets requires at least 3.5 to 4 hours at IST and 3 hours at SAW.

If your international flight arrives at IST on Turkish Airlines, book your onward domestic leg on the same single PNR ticket. That way your luggage checks straight through to your final Turkish destination (you clear passport control in Istanbul, then walk to the domestic concourse), and Turkish Airlines is legally obligated to rebook you onto the next departure if an inbound delay causes a misconnection. For separate-ticket transfers into the city first, review our [Istanbul taxi and private transfer guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/istanbul-taxi-tips-scams).

faq.q: Which Cappadocia airport is better: Kayseri (ASR) or Nevşehir (NAV)?
faq.a: Nevşehir (NAV) is closer to Göreme and Uçhisar (about 40 minutes by car) but has fewer daily flights. Kayseri (ASR) is roughly 65–75 minutes away and offers far more daily departures on Turkish Airlines, Pegasus, and AJet.

faq.q: Does Turkish Airlines serve free snacks on domestic flights?
faq.a: Yes. Turkish Airlines still includes complimentary hot toasted sandwiches or pastries plus tea, coffee, or juice on domestic economy flights, whereas Pegasus and AJet sell food and drinks on board.

faq.q: Can I buy extra domestic baggage weight online after booking?
faq.a: Yes. All three airlines let you add extra checked kilos through their websites or mobile apps up to a few hours before departure at significantly lower rates than airport check-in counters.

faq.q: How early should I arrive for a domestic flight at IST or SAW?
faq.a: Arrive at least 90 minutes before departure at SAW and 2 hours before departure at IST. Both airports require a terminal entrance security scan before check-in plus a second airside security check, and walking distances at IST are long.

faq.q: Are domestic flights in Türkiye frequently delayed?
faq.a: Morning departures are generally punctual, while late-afternoon and evening rotations on Pegasus and AJet can pick up 30-to-60-minute knock-on delays during peak summer months. Avoid booking the very last flight of the night before a morning hot-air balloon or international departure.

faq.q: Do I need my physical passport for domestic flights in Türkiye?
faq.a: Yes. Foreign travelers must present their original physical passport at check-in and boarding gates for every domestic flight in Türkiye; photocopies or smartphone photos are not accepted.
